name: prime-host positions as word indices into the texts
idea: The DBBI prime scaffold's 31 host positions (and the 60 complementary payload positions) are used as 1-based word indices into the Architect 3.2.1 text and the final page's decoded strings, taking whole words, their initials and their final letters. The page phrase 'yellowblueprimes' plus 'itsinfrontofyoureyesbutyourenotseeingit' license reading the prime scaffold as a pointer into text already on the page rather than as a cipher over DBBI itself. The mask is also stepped in 91-word windows so it can reach past the first 91 words.
check: Each returned string is tried as a passphrase against the SALPH 'Salted__' blob and the other final-page blobs; a successful OpenSSL AES decrypt to readable text confirms it.
retro: Stage 0: positions in the spiral walk select which cells carry meaning (the 24 coloured cells sit on byte boundaries), i.e. position-driven selection over a fixed stream.

name: payload digits as letter-index inside successive words
idea: Each a-i symbol is read as a value 1-9 and used as the within-word letter index of the k-th word of the target text (a tap-code/book-cipher read), for DBBI, the 83-parse payload, the host letters and three 200-symbol FAED windows. This is text extraction, not a cipher over the symbol stream: the symbols only say which letter of an existing word to take. 'Its in front of your eyes but youre not seeing it' licenses letting the a-i stream point at the visible prose.
check: Passphrase trial against the SALPH blob and the other encrypted final-page material; also scanned for private-key shapes against the prize and halving addresses.
retro: Stage 3: the sixth component was a hex string that had to be decoded into text, i.e. numeric symbols standing for characters to be read off.

name: digits as cumulative skips along words and letters
idea: Instead of indexing absolutely, the a-i values are read as gaps: start at 0 and advance by each value, harvesting the word or letter landed on. Applied to the Architect text, the Stage 3.2.2 answer and the page strings, for the DBBI stream, the 83-parse payload and the whole FAED stream. The puzzle's 'one for one, four for one' and the prime-gap structure of the scaffold both describe stepping, not addressing.
check: Passphrase trial against the final-page 'Salted__' blobs; confirmation is a clean AES-256-CBC decrypt.
retro: Stage 0: the spiral walk advances a fixed number of cells per byte, harvesting the cell landed on.

name: last and first words around named anchors and equal segments
idea: Direct reading of the page string 'lastwordsbeforearchichoice': collect the word immediately before (and after) every occurrence of CHOICE, KEY, KEYNOTE, PRIME, LAST, SOURCE, ONE, CODE, PASSWORD, TRUE, ANSWER, QUESTION in the Architect text and page strings, and also the last word of each of N equal segments and of each line, for N in the puzzle's own counts 7, 13, 14, 16, 23, 24, 30, 31, 91. The page names this operation in words, so it is the most literally licensed extraction on the final page.
check: Passphrase trial against SALPH and the Stage 3.2 leftover 'Salted__' blob; a readable decrypt confirms.
retro: Stage 2: the answer 'causality' was obtained by reading the URL sentence as a sentence and naming the thing it describes, i.e. word-level reading rather than symbol transformation.

name: FAED as a nine-lane mask over the Architect letter stream
idea: Align FAED's 570 symbols one-to-one with the first 570 letters (and separately the first 570 words) of the Architect text and keep only the positions carrying a given symbol, giving nine lanes plus the checkerboard escape pairs g,i and b,e. FAED is used purely as a stencil over existing text, which is the untested direction: previous work decoded FAED as ciphertext rather than treating it as a mask on the prose.
check: Passphrase trial against the final-page blobs; also key-shape scan against the prize address.
retro: Stage 0: blue/yellow classes act as a mask selecting which spiral cells are meaningful.

name: image spiral geometry as text coordinates
idea: The 25 events of the first image carry row, column and spiral index; these become indices into the Architect text: row*14+column as a word index, the spiral index as a letter index, and row or column alone as small indices, with blue and yellow events read as two separate phrases. The image is the puzzle's own coordinate system and 'yellowblueprimes' says the two colours split the reading.
check: Passphrase trial against SALPH; a readable AES decrypt, or a returned 64-hex/WIF matching the prize address.
retro: Stage 0: the same spiral coordinates were the mechanism that produced the first URL.

name: one-for-one four-for-one take-and-skip extraction
idea: Stage 3.2's line 'One for one, four for one' and the straddling checkerboard's escape digits 1 and 4 are read as an extraction rhythm: keep positions 1 and 4 of every group of five (also of four, ten and fourteen), and take one item then skip four (and the inverse), over both the word stream and the letter stream of the Architect text, the answer and the page strings.
check: Passphrase trial against the final-page 'Salted__' blobs.
retro: Stage 3.2.2: digits 1 and 4 were the working escape digits of the straddling checkerboard, so the puzzle already used that pair as a selector.

name: the 91-mask applied to the macro phrase chain
idea: The reversed-binary macro phrase list is concatenated into a single letter stream and the 31 host positions / 60 payload positions of the DBBI scaffold are applied to it (and to the answer, and to both concatenated), with the 91-window repeated along the whole string; host ranks also select whole macro phrases, and host positions select the same-ranked letter inside each phrase. The macro list is the page's own ordered text, so it is the natural body for the page's own mask.
check: Passphrase trial against SALPH and the other encrypted blobs.
retro: Stage 3: seven separate answers were concatenated in a fixed order into one string before hashing.

name: Bifid BTCSEED output as book-cipher coordinates
idea: The Bifid reading of FAED is dominated by B, C, D, E, which look like small coordinate values; take its letters as A=1..Z=26 and read consecutive pairs as (word number, letter within word) into the Architect text and the other texts, plus the single values as absolute and cumulative letter indices. This treats the Bifid tail as a pointer list into prose rather than as key material, which the already-tested list explicitly leaves open.
check: Passphrase trial against the final-page blobs; the leading BTCSEED plus a readable extraction would be visible confirmation.
retro: Stage 3.2.1: Bifid/coordinate pair reading of a two-digit-per-letter square was already the mechanism that produced this string.

name: run lengths and equal-chunk acrostics
idea: Run lengths of equal consecutive symbols in DBBI and FAED (a property of the streams that no previous phase used) become word/letter indices and cumulative skips into the texts; separately the Architect text, the answer and the page strings are cut into 7, 13, 14, 16, 23, 24, 30, 31 and 91 equal blocks and the first and last letter of each block are read off as an acrostic.
check: Passphrase trial against the SALPH blob and companions.
retro: Stage 1: the answer was a single line lifted whole out of a longer text once the clues said which line, i.e. block-level selection.
